questionText:
A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of length $13\text{ cm}$ and one of the other sides of length $5\text{ cm}$.

(a) Find the length of the third side.
(b) Find, correct to one decimal place, the size of the angle opposite the $5\text{ cm}$ side.
markingScheme:
(a) Apply Pythagoras' Theorem: $13^2 - 5^2 = 144$; third side $= 12\text{ cm}$ **(2 marks)**
(b) Use $\sin\theta = \frac{5}{13}$ **(1 mark)**
Compute $\theta = \sin^{-1}(5/13) \approx 22.6°$ **(2 marks)**

solutionSteps.explanation: Let the third side be $x$. Then $13^2 = 5^2 + x^2$, so $x^2 = 169 - 25 = 144$ and $x = 12\text{ cm}$.
The angle opposite the $5\text{ cm}$ side has $\sin\theta = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \dfrac{5}{13}$.
